provider: Texas Department of Insurance (TDI) — Basic Manual of Rules, Rates, and Forms for the Writing of Title Insurance in the State of Texas (REGULATORY/PROMULGATED, not provider-set)
sourceUrl: https://www.tdi.texas.gov/orders/documents/20259697.pdf (Commissioner's Order No. 2025-9697, Exhibit A rate table) and https://www.tdi.texas.gov/rules/2025/documents/2026titlerateprop.pdf (rule adoption); premium table cross-verified against two independent provider republications: https://www.republictitle.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Residential-Title-Rates.pdf and https://www.independencetitle.com/wp-content/uploads/pdfs/TitleRates_March2026.pdf
asOf: Order signed 2025-12-19; rates effective 2026-03-01 (a 6.2% reduction from the prior Order No. 2019-5980 schedule)

settlementFee.note: TITLE INSURANCE PREMIUMS in Texas are fixed by the Insurance Commissioner under Tex. Ins. Code ch. 2703 and are UNIFORM across every title company/agent in the state -- this is not a provider-set price and is included here for regulatory context, not as a 'good source' on the settlement-fee side. Basic (Owner's Policy) premium table effective 3/1/2026, exact figures from Exhibit A: $25,000 liability = $308; $50,000 = $465; $100,000 = $780; $200,000 = $1,274 (per Republic Title's and Independence Title's own March-2026 republications of the identical TDI table); $300,000 = $1,768; $400,000 = $2,262; $500,000 = $2,756; $1,000,000 = $5,226.
settlementFee.cplFee: Texas Insurance Code Sec. 2702.001(c): 'A title insurance company may not impose a charge for issuing insured closing and settlement letters under this section.' The Insured Closing Letter (ICL, Texas's equivalent of a CPL, Form T-50/T-51) is therefore promulgated at $0 -- issued 'incidentally to title insurance at no additional cost' (confirmed independently by First Texas Title's own site, see separate entry below, and by National Investors Title Insurance Company's Texas Underwriting Manual, which states the ICL 'provides additional coverage for certain escrow matters at no cost'). No exact fee amount is stated anywhere in the Basic Manual because none may be charged.
settlementFee.guarantyFee: State of Texas Title Insurance Guaranty Association (TTIGA) Policy Guaranty Fee: $2.00 per owner's policy and $2.00 per loan policy issued (in effect since 5/1/2019), increasing to $3.00 per policy for closings after 9/30/2026 per TLTA Compliance Update (https://tlta.com/TLTA/News_Articles/Compliance_Update_Guaranty_Fee_Increasing_Starting_Oct_1_2026.aspx) and TTIGA (https://ttiga.org/guaranty-fees/). This fee is paid by the consumer and shown on the settlement statement; it funds TDI's title-agent audit function and agent-insolvency costs. Independently corroborated at $2.00/policy on two provider fee sheets fetched this session (Patten Title and Texas National Title, see below).

bundlingNotes: TX is a file-and-use / commissioner-fixed-rate state: the basic premium is identical for every title insurance company and every title agent in Texas at a given liability amount and effective date -- confirmed by three independently fetched, differently-branded documents (TDI's own Commissioner's Order, Republic Title's March-2026 rate card, and Independence Title's March-2026 rate card) all showing numerically identical figures ($780 at $100,000, $2,262 at $400,000, $5,226 at $1,000,000, etc.). Because the premium is fixed, it carries NO market signal about provider quality or competitiveness -- the settlement/escrow/service-fee side (documented in the entries below) is the only place where TX title companies actually compete on price, and it varies enormously by provider, as the entries below demonstrate.
transactionContext: Applies uniformly to Owner's Policy and Loan Policy premiums statewide, all metros, all provider types (national-brand underwriters, independent agents, attorneys). Not applicable to purchase-vs-refinance distinctions -- premium calculation depends only on policy face amount, not transaction type.

bundlingNotes: Explicitly framed as a Loan-Estimate fee sheet for lenders ('For Lender Use Only'), 'good in State of Texas only' and 'good until revised' -- i.e., published specifically to support TRID/CFPB Loan Estimate compliance, distinct from a consumer-facing rate card but still a genuine provider-published, dollar-denominated settlement-fee document. Escrow fee is $50 higher for purchase than refinance, and courier fee is $10 higher for purchase, mirroring the same purchase>refinance fee-tiering pattern seen at Great American's fellow statewide independent Patten Title (though Patten prices purchase and refinance identically) and at First Texas Title.
transactionContext: Statewide Texas branch network; distinct escrow/courier figures for purchase vs. refinance transactions, plus a worked example showing how the (uniform, promulgated) title premium itself should be entered on a Loan Estimate.
